The push notifications ticket is done. PR #733 has the Kotlin changes and 9 passing tests, and build 412 is on internal testing. Someone needs to approve the new notification permission before it goes wider.

Trial signups from Germany fell 38% since Tuesday while every other country held steady. No monitor covers this. It started with PR #4821, which changed the VAT field on the signup form, so Maya is the likely owner.

Last night: 42 experiments, 5 kept, 36 discarded, 1 crashed. Validation loss dropped from 1.83 to 1.71, mostly from a cosine learning rate and a larger batch size. The kept changes are on the autoresearch branch.

Launch update: the pricing page is done, and the docs have been waiting on Sam's review since Monday. I handed the failing Safari test to your QA engineer and will check on it at 3 pm. Nothing else is blocking Thursday's release.

This month I opened 5 small pull requests: one patches a high-severity CVE in axios, two remove flags that reached 100% of users, and two replace deprecated APIs. Each shows the passing tests and why it's safe to merge.

This week I opened 3 pull requests that remove 1,240 lines nothing uses, including the old billing export. Tests pass and no callers remain. I left legacy_webhooks.py alone because a cron job calls it by name.

PR #5060 has one bug to fix before merging: at line 88 of payments/refund.py, a partial refund uses the full order total, so customers would get back too much. I left a comment with the fix on that line.

Password resets live in auth/reset.py, lines 40 to 92. The token is signed, lasts 30 minutes and works once, which line 67 enforces. I read the code but didn't check the production config, which could change the expiry.
SOC 2 control CC8.1 no longer holds: branch protection was turned off on the payments repo, and 2 pull requests reached main without review. Evidence for the other 31 controls is current.

Annual plans made up 41% of new revenue in October, up from 33% in September. The chart and query are attached. One caveat: 12 enterprise deals paid by invoice haven't synced yet, so the real number may be higher.
Devin got stuck 14 times this week, and 9 of them had the same cause: it couldn't start the local database. Adding make db-up to its setup should stop these. I drafted the change for you to approve.
This week's awards: night owl goes to Priya for a 3:12 am fix to the retry logic. Hot potato is checkout.ts, changed by 9 people. Fossil is a 2017 date helper that still runs on every invoice.
Your refund tool is live. Support can look up an order and refund up to $200, and larger refunds go to a manager. The video shows it working, and I'll keep it running. Tell me what to change.
The saved searches ticket is done. PR #812 has the SwiftUI screen and 6 passing UI tests, and build 214 is on TestFlight. It needs your approval before it goes to external testers.
GET /orders caused the most waiting this week, at 1,840 ms p95. Most of that was an N+1 query on line items. PR #4933 batches it and brings p95 down to 310 ms in the same benchmark.

Moving to the new payments API: 31 of 48 pull requests merged, none rolled back. The refunds batch is blocked because its webhook tests need a sandbox key. Add the key and the last 17 can ship by Friday.

The 2:32 pm API alert most likely comes from PR #5044, deployed 12 minutes earlier, which cut the database pool from 50 connections to 5. The logs show 1,200 connection timeouts since then. PR #5046 reverts it and is ready for you.

Every event is an HTTPS POST with a JSON body and Standard Webhooks signature headers, sent to the URL you register. One handler receives everything and branches on event_type — it only needs to do three things:

When you add an endpoint (or change its URL, re-enable it, or click Verify) we immediately POST an endpoint.verification event whose data.nonce you must echo back: respond 2xx with that exact nonce in the body, e.g. {"nonce": "…"}. This is the only event that needs an echo — every other event just needs a 2xx. Until it passes, the endpoint stays pending and receives no events.

Each request carries webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature headers. Compute HMAC-SHA256 over {webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body} with your signing secret (base64-decode the part after whsec_) and compare it with the space-separated v1,… values in the signature header — any match is valid, and there are several while a secret rotation is in progress.

Return a 2xx within 10 seconds; anything else is retried with backoff for about three days, after which the endpoint is disabled. Retries and replays reuse the same webhook-id, so treat a repeated ID as already handled.
